results.evidence: Central warrant (Ps.2.10-12 imperative-address strophe closing on an ashrei inclusio with Ps.1.1) is sound and its digit-bearing claims re-derive true from verse_map_oshb.json: Ps.2.12 has exactly 14 words, אַ֖שְׁרֵ֗י is word 11, and exactly 3 words follow it (כָּל ח֥וֹסֵי בֽוֹ) -- matches the row's 'word 11 of 14 ... three words following' claim. Dual-cites (web:Ps.2.11=oshb:Ps.2.11, web:Ps.2.12=oshb:Ps.2.12, web:Ps.1.1=oshb:Ps.1.1) all validate under citation_sweep.py (status GREEN, 0 problems; Ps.2 and Ps.1 are identity psalms so 1:1 numbering is correct). BUT: citation_sweep.py flags 2 nfd_degraded hits in device_notes, and manual codepoint comparison against verse_map_oshb.json confirms both are real byte-level corruptions, not tool noise: (1) the quoted אַ֖שְׁרֵ֗י (claimed oshb:Ps.2.12) has its shin-dot (U+05C1) and sheva (U+05B0) combining marks TRANSPOSED versus source order (source: ...05e9,05c1,05b0... ; row: ...05e9,05b0,05c1...); (2) the quoted אַ֖שְֽׁרֵ֗י (claimed oshb:Ps.1.1) has shin-dot/sheva/meteg (U+05C1/U+05B0/U+05BD) permuted versus source order (source: shin-dot,sheva,meteg ; row: sheva,meteg,shin-dot). Both quotes are visually identical to source and collate at NFD tier only, not BYTE tier, which the book's own rule set requires for any pointed Hebrew quotation ('a pointed run whose best tier is nfd is NOT a pass' -- TOOLKIT.md citation_sweep.py spec, confirmed live in this run's JSON output: nfd_degraded_count=2 for M8-Ps-005). This is exactly the copy-degradation hazard the toolkit warns never hand-type/copy-through pointed Hebrew. Cure: re-splice both tokens programmatically from verse_map_oshb.json via normalize_hebrew_in_json.py --write and re-collate. Everything else in the row (meteg-difference claim, 1-of-4-tiers skeleton-match claim, rejected_alternative, boundary_evidence_refs) checks out.
